what_where.text: Warrumbungle National Park is near Coonabarabran in NSW, about 550 km north-west of Sydney, 23,311 ha, based on the Warrumbungle Mountain Range (remnants of a volcano). Australia's first Dark Sky Park (certified 4 July 2016 by the International Dark-Sky Association). Added to the National Heritage List December 2006 for bold volcanic landforms 'unrivalled anywhere else in Australia'. Reserved 1953.

formations.text: Well-known formations: Belougery Spire, Bluff Mountain, Mount Exmouth (tallest in the park), the Breadknife, Split Rock, Fans Horizon, Crater Bluff. The Breadknife towers 90 m above the valley floor and is the park's most recognisable feature (NPWS).

walk.text: Breadknife and Grand High Tops walk: 14.5 km loop, 5-6 hrs suggested, Grade 4, starts at Pincham car park south of John Renshaw Parkway; follows Spirey Creek, climbs past Belougery Spire, Bress Peak and Crater Bluff, Balor Hut campground, Grand High Tops, Dows Camp with Bluff Mountain views; shorter 12.5 km return via Dagda Shortcut. Spring wildflowers; wedge-tailed eagles, peregrine falcons. Shorter option: Fans Horizon track from the same car park to a lookout over the Breadknife, Belougery Spire and Crater Bluff. Free Personal Locator Beacon hire at Warrumbungle Visitor Centre. Bring water, hat, sunscreen.

observatory.text: Siding Spring Observatory sits atop Mt Woorut (~1160 m) at the end of Observatory Road, 27 km west of Coonabarabran on the park's eastern edge. Open to the public 7 days, 8:30 am-4:00 pm; Cafe and Exploratory closed Tuesdays; AAT Visitor Gallery open 7 days; guided tours via Coonabarabran Stargazing (0488 687 562). NOT open at night for public viewing (working research facility). Closed in extreme fire danger. No caravans on the access road. Officially opened 1965, built on the park boundary partly for its dark skies.
observatory.note: Wikivoyage says guided tours in NSW school holidays and an annual October Open Day (updated Aug 2021); the operator page says tours via Coonabarabran Stargazing. Use the operator wording.

dark_sky.text: NPWS: 'zero light pollution'; star charts sold at the Warrumbungle Visitor Centre; good for stargazing, amateur astronomy and camping under the stars.

fire_2013.text: About 80% of the park burned in January 2013 (visitor centre, railings and platforms destroyed); facilities have since been rebuilt (NPWS says walking tracks, campgrounds and visitor sites rebuilt). Wikipedia: koalas thought wiped out.

visitor_centre.text: Warrumbungle NP Visitor Information Centre, 4261 John Renshaw Parkway, 02 6825 4364, 9am-4pm daily, closed Christmas Day. (Wikivoyage, Oct 2021, shows closed noon-1pm: unverified now.)

get_in.text: Coonabarabran side is 27 km of sealed John Renshaw Parkway (Wikipedia); NPWS directions say approx. 35 km from Coonabarabran town streets. West side via Coonamble has unsealed sections. No places to eat in the park: bring your own food.
get_in.note: Distance figures differ (27 vs ~35 km); avoid a precise number or say 'about 30 km'.

goodToKnow_candidates.tip: Park entry is $8 per vehicle per day (annual and Country NSW passes also valid per Wikivoyage); the park is always open but can close for poor weather or fire danger, so check NPWS alerts before driving out.

Siding Spring Observatory is open 8:30 am-4 pm daily (cafe closed Tuesdays) but not at night; it closes on extreme fire-danger days, and caravans can't use the narrow access road. For night viewing book a Coonabarabran Stargazing tour.

Summers often top 30C (record 42.6C) and winter nights drop below freezing; no food is sold in the park, so carry water, hat, sunscreen and food. For the Grade 4 High Tops loop allow 5-6 hrs and borrow a free PLB at the visitor centre.
